svg.title: Figure 4. Superclass removal
svg.desc: Figure 4. Dumbbell chart of flow capacity lost when every cell type of one superclass is removed, each against the mean of 200 random sets of the same size: descending 66.4% against 8.2%, nerve cord sensory 50.1% against 2.9%, central brain intrinsic 49.3% against 82.4%, nerve cord intrinsic 47.0% against 42.9%, ascending 34.7% against 9.7%, central brain sensory 32.5% against 2.7%, nerve cord motor 16.6% against 2.4%, sensory ascending 13.6% against 0.4%, optic lobe intrinsic 0.6% against 4.7%, central brain motor 0.4% against 0.7%, visual projection 0.4% against 5.9%, visual centrifugal 0.1% against 1.8%, nerve cord efferent 0.0% against 0.4%. Classes that hold sensory or motor terminal types lose far more than random, as expected. Among the others, ascending neurons lose 34.7% against 9.7%, p = 0.005, while central brain intrinsic neurons lose 49.3% against 82.4%.
